questions.question: What is a storyboard?
choices: A sequence of sketches planning shots or scenes

questions.question: Why use storyboards before filming or animation?
choices: They help plan sequence, framing, and visual transitions

questions.question: What does a shot list record?
What information can arrows in a storyboard communicate?
choices: Movement of a subject or camera

questions.question: What is an establishing shot used for?
choices: Show a location or context before closer action

questions.question: How can a close-up support storytelling?
choices: It always shows the full setting
It emphasizes a detail, expression, or reaction
It sets the scene's total duration

questions.question: What is a point-of-view shot?
choices: A shot of the camera operator
A view from the audience only
A view framed as if seen by a character

questions.question: Why should a storyboard consider screen direction?
choices: Consistent movement helps viewers follow where characters are going

questions.question: A sequence feels confusing because characters seem to switch places. What could a storyboard clarify?
choices: Their positions, movement, and camera angle across shots

questions.question: How does a visual motif help tell a story?
choices: A recurring image can connect moments or develop meaning

questions.question: What is a transition in visual storytelling?
choices: A change from one shot, scene, or moment to another

questions.question: Why vary shot size in a sequence?
choices: Every story requires one shot size
Different shot sizes provide context, action, or detail

questions.question: What can a storyboard reveal about pacing?
choices: Whether key moments have enough visual time and progression

questions.question: What is a match cut?
choices: A cut made only during dialogue
A transition connecting shots through a visual or conceptual similarity
An edit that removes all movement

questions.question: How can a storyboard show an emotional change without dialogue?
choices: Use pose, framing, gesture, and visual context

questions.question: Why include notes about sound in a storyboard?
choices: Sound cues can shape timing and meaning alongside images

questions.question: A reveal should surprise viewers. What could the storyboard plan?
choices: Control what is visible before the reveal and when the new information appears
Show the reveal in every earlier frame
Use the same wide shot throughout

questions.question: What is visual continuity?
choices: A rule that every shot be identical
Consistent details that help shots feel connected

questions.question: How can a creator make storyboards accessible to collaborators?
choices: Use clear labels, readable sketches, and concise production notes

questions.question: Why revise a storyboard after feedback?
choices: It proves the first idea was wrong
It can expose unclear action or missing visual information before production
